transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Lauren Kim (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Marcus Hale (CISO), Priya Rao (Head of Platform), Ian Cho (SRE)

[00:00] Lauren Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lauren from Redwood, and Ravi is our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Marcus Hale: Good, thanks. Busy day, but, yeah, excited to get into this.
[00:10] Priya Rao: Hi all. Quick background: we're evaluating options for hosting LLMs for our fraud-detection assistants; main ask is no PII leakage and strict retention.
[00:18] Lauren Kim: Totally, that's what we're here for. We'll do a quick qual, then Ravi will cover technical posture around SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/ encryption, and deployment modes.
[00:27] Ian Cho: Quick note — our infra team is leaning toward Dedicated or Private because of compliance, but cost is a concern.
[00:33] Ravi Patel: Understood. I'll start with compliance posture: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and we also maintain ISO 27001 summary; I'll send the certs after the call. Our hosted environment is SOC2-covered; Private gives you a private control plane and can sit in your VPC for added isolation.
[00:49] Marcus Hale: For Private, do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)? We need to ensure Redwood never has access to plaintext keys.
[00:56] Ravi Patel: Yes — we support BYOK via cloud KMS integrations and HSM in on-prem options. In hosted mode we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default, but you can swap to your KMS. There's an audit trail for key ops.
[01:06] Priya Rao: Can you be more specific about audit logs? We need immutable logs for access to model artifacts, who called the endpoint, and any admin changes. Retention must be configurable for up to 7 years.
[01:17] Ravi Patel: Audit logs capture token-level requests, admin events, role changes. Logs are streamed to customer S3 or SIEM via our log-exporter; retention is configurable. Long-term retention we typically do via customer-managed archival (e.g., to their S3 with lifecycle rules). There are a couple of buts—some very granular debug traces are ephemeral and kept short for performance reasons.
[01:35] Marcus Hale: Ok — do those logs include inputs and outputs? We can't store full PII in our environment for over 30 days.
[01:41] Lauren Kim: There's a couple of options — you can enable redaction and prefix-only caching so that sensitive inputs are never persisted. For hosted, you can configure tokenization/redaction rules; for Dedicated/Private you control retention and logs entirely.
[01:52] Ian Cho: When you say redaction, is that automatic or do we need to post-process?
[01:56] Ravi Patel: We have a built-in data masking pipeline that can do regex-based redaction pre-ingest. It's configurable and you can add transforms. We also recommend doing application-side PII stripping as best practice.
[02:08] Priya Rao: SSO — we run Okta, Duo for MFA. How does enterprise SSO / SAML work?
[02:13] Ravi Patel: We integrate with SAML 2.0 providers, Okta, Azure AD. SSO provisioning supports SCIM for user/group sync and role mapping. RBAC maps to OAuth scopes and resource-level permissions; you can restrict per-route or per-model.
[02:26] Marcus Hale: Can we map groups so that only certain teams can call specific models and also have read-only viewers for logs?
[02:31] Ravi Patel: Yes, group-based RBAC maps into role sets — you can create policies like model-call, model-admin, logs-viewer. All admin actions are logged.
[02:39] Ian Cho: How about secrets management — do you rotate keys automatically?
[02:43] Ravi Patel: For Redwood-managed keys we rotate per our schedule; for customer KMS, rotation is under your control. We support automatic key rotation for some KMS providers via APIs.
[02:53] Priya Rao: Are there FedRAMP /CCPA considerations? We are primarily US/EU; need data residency in us-east and eu-west regions.
[02:59] Lauren Kim: We can pin region for dedicated/private deployments. Hosted customers can choose region endpoints; we are working on formalized FedRAMP packaging but not out-of-the-box. For most financial customers we recommend Dedicated for strict residency + SLA.
[03:12] Marcus Hale: About model artifacts — if we upload custom models or fine-tuned checkpoints, who has access?
[03:17] Ravi Patel: Access is tenancy-based. With Dedicated and Private, artifacts live in your isolated storage. For hosted, artifacts are tenant-scoped; only authorized admins in your org can access them. We do not share between tenants.
[03:27] Marcus Hale: Ok. Any details on vulnerability management and pen tests?
[03:30] Ravi Patel: We run quarterly internal scans, annual third-party pentests, and patch management. We can share summary reports in the security pack.
[03:37] Priya Rao: On data retention — we need to ensure that logs, KV caches, and any trace of user inputs are deleted on request within a SLA. Can Redwood support deletion requests?
[03:47] Lauren Kim: Yes. We have purge APIs and a documented process for data deletion. For hosted, deletion requests go through our control plane; we provide certs of deletion for specific datasets. For Dedicated/Private, you own storage so you can enforce deletion yourself.
[03:59] Ian Cho: You mentioned KV cache earlier — is KV cache persisted to disk and does it contain user prompts?
[04:04] Ravi Patel: The KV cache stores key/value states for decoding — by default we keep session prefixes in memory and, for longer sessions, we checkpoint to encrypted storage. We have options to not persist prefixes or to store only hashed prefixes. We recommend not storing raw prompts for PII workloads.
[04:17] Marcus Hale: Good. What about certifications — you said SOC2 Type II and ISO. Can you share the scope of SOC2? Is it limited to hosting or does it include product infra and change management?
[04:27] Ravi Patel: SOC2 scope covers hosting, customer data handling in the control plane, incident management, and change mgmt for the runtime. We'll attach the SOC2 report; redactions may apply for sensitive pages.
[04:39] Priya Rao: SLA — what uptime / latency guarantees do you have for Dedicated? We need 99.95% and P99 latency targets for small inference calls.
[04:48] Ravi Patel: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime at 99.95% for the cluster and configurable P99 latency targets depending on pool size and profile. We'll provide the SLA doc in the follow-up.
[04:58] Marcus Hale: If we start in Hosted then move to Dedicated, how smooth is migration — do you support seamless model/version pinning?
[05:04] Lauren Kim: Yes, deployment abstraction is one of our strengths — same API across modes, you can pin model versions and redirect traffic via routing policies. We also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to hosted if dedicated capacity is exhausted (depending on contract).
[05:17] Ian Cho: About cost — can you provide a high-level on what drives cost between Hosted and Dedicated?
[05:21] Ravi Patel: Key drivers: per-token compute, model size/quantization, reserved GPU pool costs, and additional features like higher retention or long-term logs export. Dedicated reduces per-token marginal cost at the expense of committed capacity. Optimize suggests specific quantization profiles.
[05:34] Marcus Hale: One more — for enterprise audits we need traceability: who approved model access, when keys rotated, and admin changes. Are those available in the audit trail?
[05:42] Ravi Patel: Yes — admin events, approvals, key rotations, and role changes are emitted as auditable events with timestamps and actor identity. These can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[05:50] Priya Rao: Any blockers we should be aware of for on-prem Private deployments? Network egress rules, HSM integrations — what's the typical timeline?
[05:58] Ravi Patel: Typical private deployment takes 8-12 weeks for standard setups — longer if you need air-gapped HSMs or heavy customization. We'll surface the pre-reqs — VPN, firewall rules, and storage provisioning.
[06:10] Lauren Kim: Ok, want to recap next steps? We'll send SOC2 + ISO summary, security pack, and the SLA/Pricing sheet. Ravi will set up a perf benchmark session. Marcus will share retention/KMS requirements.
[06:22] Marcus Hale: Sounds good. Also please include a short checklist for compliance reviewers.
[06:26] Lauren Kim: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[06:30] Priya Rao: Thanks — talk soon.
[06:32] Ian Cho: Thanks.

Notes: occasional transcription errors: "K V cache" appears in raw transcript; "Redwood Dedi" heard in one place. Shared artifacts referenced: /links/Redwood_SOC2_TypeII.pdf, /links/redwood-security-pack.zip, /links/dedicated-pricing.xlsx.
